두 사람이 각자 양손에 가위, 바위, 보 중 하나씩을 동시에 낸다. 두: Two people each throw one of scissors, rock, or paper with each of their two hands at the same time. They may throw the same thing with both hands. Then the two people each withdraw one hand at the same time, and the single remaining hands compete against each other. Paper beats scissors, scissors beats rock, rock beats paper. If the remaining hands are the same, it is a tie.

Two people each throw one of scissors, rock, or paper with each of their two hands at the same time. They may throw the same thing with both hands. Then the two people each withdraw one hand at the same time, and the single remaining hands compete against each other. Scissors beats paper, rock beats scissors, paper beats rock. If the remaining hands are the same, it is a tie.
나는 바위와 보를 냈고, 상대는 보와 바위를 냈다. 한 손씩 뺀 뒤 나는: I threw rock and paper, and the opponent threw paper and rock. After each withdrew one hand, I kept paper and the opponent kept rock.
나는 보와 바위를 냈고, 상대는 보와 보를 냈다. 한 손씩 뺀 뒤 나는: I threw paper and rock, and the opponent threw paper and paper. After each withdrew one hand, I kept rock and the opponent kept paper.
나는 가위와 보를 냈고, 상대는 가위와 가위를 냈다. 상대가 가위를 남긴: I threw scissors and paper, and the opponent threw scissors and scissors. I know that the opponent will keep scissors.
내가 지려면 어느 손을 남겨야 하는가?: Which hand must I keep in order to lose?
I threw scissors and rock, and the opponent threw scissors and paper.
상대가 어느 손을 남길지 모른다. 어떤 경우에도 지지 않으려면 나는 어느: I do not know which hand the opponent will keep. Which hand must I keep in order not to lose in any case?
I threw rock and paper, and the opponent threw scissors and rock.
